subset_recommendation.evidence_and_rationale: Days 1–30 is recommended as the smallest complete evaluation candidate for the following reasons: 1. Complete Red-Team Label Coverage: Exactly 100% of all red-team compromise records (749 of 749 rows, and 715 of 715 unique labels across 18 distinct compromise days) fall entirely within Days 1–30. Days 31–58 contain zero red-team events in the LANL dataset. 2. Chronological Separation for Validation and Testing: Days 1–30 provides multiple distinct attack waves (e.g., initial compromise and early lateral movement in Days 2–16, intermediate campaigns in Days 21–23, and final active persistence/movement in Days 27–30). This allows Member 4 and the team in Task 2.3 to formulate clean, non-overlapping chronological validation and test partitions without sacrificing any labels. 3. Rich Behavioral and Rolling Graph Warm-Up History: Day 1 provides uncompromised baseline activity, followed by interspersed attack and high-volume background activity, giving sufficient history for graph autoencoder snapshots and GRU sequence context. 4. Substantial Reduction in Local Processing Burden: Restricting to Days 1–30 cuts total dataset volume from 1,051,430,459 rows (73.41 GB) down to 508,854,306 rows (32.5169 GB), retaining 100% of labels while eliminating 51.60% of raw unlabelled processing cost. While Days 1–16 captures 91.99% of red-team rows, it prematurely truncates the final 4 labelled attack days (Days 21, 22, 23, 27, 28, 29, 30), precluding evaluation on the later multi-hop lateral movement campaigns.
subset_recommendation.boundary_coordination_note: Split boundaries (training, validation, test) are not finalized here in accordance with Task 2.1 scope, as split design belongs to Task 2.3 and must be coordinated with Member 4. Unlabelled background activity must strictly not be treated as proven-benign.
